$meta.name: PaperMatch shared vocabularies
$meta.note: Canonical enum values shared by the TypeScript app and the Python API. Both sides load this file; tests on both sides assert parity so the vocabularies cannot drift.

paperType.$note: Section 18: 論文種別, plus the theory/experiment axis section 16 balances the feed on. `theoretical` and `experimental` are assigned by a rule-based classifier that abstains when the abstract does not say clearly, so a paper carrying neither means 'not determined', never 'neither'.

retractionStatus.$note: Section 21: withdrawal and correction state must be representable and refreshable.

abstractSection.$note: Section 8: structural roles detected in an abstract.

detectionMethod.$note: Section 8: how a structural label was produced. A rule-based pass is 'heuristic', not 'ai' — conflating them would overstate what the label is worth.

saveReason.$note: Section 9: optional tags attached on save.

expressionKind.$note: Section 9: 個人用学術英語辞典 — 単語 / 連語 / 構文 / 一文.

reviewOutcome.$note: Section 9/10: 派手な点数化はせず — only 'again' and 'got_it'.

savedStatus.$note: Section 9: reading state of a saved paper.

actionType.$note: Section 23: Action. The last five are section 16's feed feedback, and every one of them is a nudge the user can undo — section 16: 否定的フィードバックを「嫌い」と決めつけない.

reportReason.$note: Section 12: a reader saying a maths card looks wrong. Deliberately not `reviewDecision` — a reader reports a problem, a reviewer decides what to do about it. Section 27 counts these as a guardrail (AI説明の問題報告率).

reportStatus.$note: Section 12 step 10: 必要なカードのみ人手レビューへ送る.

feedReason.$note: Section 6: recommendation reasons must be explainable, never a single opaque score.

provenanceKind.$note: Section 11: origin label shown next to every formula and explanation.

verificationStatus.$note: Section 12: unverified derivations are hidden by default.

relationType.$note: Section 17: relation labels always keep their evidence.

metricSignature.$note: Section 11: never silently convert the original convention.
